units.text: It reads and writes 3D scene data in formats such as glTF, OBJ, STL, FBX, and COLLADA, converts scenes between these formats using Scene.fromFile, Scene.openFromBuffer, Scene.save, and Scene.saveToBuffer, and builds and manipulates 3D scenes through Scene, Node, Mesh, Material, Camera, and Light objects, supporting geometry construction, material assignment, and animation with keyframes.

Scene graph construction uses the Scene class as the root container, with Node instances holding Transform, optional Entity references (Mesh, Camera, or Light), and child nodes accessible through childNodes; nodes are created via Node.addChildNode, Node.addEntity, or Node.createChildNode.

Mesh geometry creation relies on the Mesh class with a controlPoints array and methods like Mesh.addControlPoint and Mesh.createPolygon to define polygonal faces, while per-vertex attribute channels such as normals (VertexElementNormal) and UVs (VertexElementUV) are attached through the VertexElement hierarchy.

Material assignment supports LambertMaterial (diffuse-only), PhongMaterial (adds specular and shininess), and PbrMaterial (metallic/roughness matching glTF 2.0 PBR), with Material.getTexture and Material.setTexture methods to manage texture references.

Camera and light entities are placed as scene nodes, with Camera exposing projectionType and fieldOfView properties, and Light supporting multiple types (POINT, DIRECTIONAL, SPOT, AREA, VOLUME) via lightType and direction properties.

Animation support uses AnimationClip to group AnimationNode tracks, each containing AnimationChannel instances with KeyframeSequence time/value samples, where KeyFrame.interpolation defines how values are interpolated between keyframes.

Format I/O reads glTF 2.0 (JSON and binary GLB) and Wavefront OBJ scenes and writes STL (ASCII and binary), FBX (ASCII), COLLADA (.dae), and glTF 2.0 JSON scenes using Scene.fromFile, Scene.open, and Scene.save, with dedicated options types for each format.

Math utilities provide FVector2, FVector3, and FVector4 vector types, Matrix4 for 4x4 transformations, Quaternion for rotations, and MathUtils for common operations, supporting geometric and transformation calculations.
The property system exposes Property and PropertyCollection types, with A3DObject.findProperty and A3DObject.setProperty methods enabling runtime inspection and modification of object properties.

Aspose.3D FOSS for TypeScript provides the @aspose/3d package (version 24.12.0) with Scene as the primary entry point for loading, saving, and manipulating 3D scenes. Scene.open, Scene.fromFile, and Scene.openFromBuffer load files or buffers, Scene.save and Scene.saveToBuffer write output, and Scene.rootNode exposes the node hierarchy for scene graph operations.

Scene serves as the root container for a 3D scene, supporting loading via Scene.open, Scene.openFromBuffer, and Scene.fromFile, and saving via Scene.save and Scene.saveToBuffer; it exposes Scene.rootNode for the node hierarchy and Scene.animationClips, Scene.createAnimationClip, and Scene.getAnimationClip for managing animation clips.

Node represents a named node in the scene tree, providing Scene.rootNode access to the hierarchy, with Node.addChildNode, Node.addEntity, Node.createChildNode, Node.childNodes, Node.entities, Node.entity, Node.globalTransform, Node.transform, and Node.material for building and inspecting the scene graph.

Mesh provides geometry data with Mesh.addControlPoint, Mesh.createPolygon, Mesh.controlPoints, Mesh.vertexElements, Mesh.getVertexElementOfUV, and Mesh.triangulate for constructing and inspecting polygonal geometry.
Material, LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, and PbrMaterial support Material.getTexture and Material.setTexture for managing surface properties on nodes.
AnimationClip, AnimationNode, AnimationChannel, KeyframeSequence, and KeyFrame support animation data management through Scene.createAnimationClip and Scene.getAnimationClip on Scene.
FileFormat supports format detection and registration via FileFormat.canImport, FileFormat.canExport, FileFormat.getFormatByExtension, and FileFormat.registerFormat.
Camera exposes Camera.projectionType, Camera.fieldOfView, Camera.nearPlane, and Camera.farPlane for configuring camera properties.
Light exposes Light.lightType, Light.direction, and Light.fieldOfView for configuring light properties.
Quaternion supports Quaternion.normalize, Quaternion.slerp, and Quaternion.toString for quaternion operations.
Matrix4 supports Matrix4.identity, Matrix4.concatenate, and Matrix4.inverse for matrix operations.
Property and PropertyCollection support A3DObject.findProperty and A3DObject.setProperty for custom property management.
FileSystem supports FileSystem.readFile and FileSystem.writeFile for file I/O operations.
Aspose.3D FOSS for TypeScript reads and writes 3D scenes using formats such as OBJ, STL, GLTF, and others; it provides basic scene construction, node hierarchy, and mesh entities.
Rendering is not implemented in this FOSS build — Scene.render throws an error.
Mesh Boolean operations (union, difference, intersect), optimize, and isManifold all throw Error('... is not implemented') in this FOSS build.
VertexElement.setIndices and VertexElement.clear throw Error('... is not implemented') in this FOSS build.
Node.selectSingleObject and Node.selectObjects throw Error('... is not implemented') in this FOSS build.
The FileSystem virtualization abstraction (readFile, writeFile, createZipFileSystem, createLocalFileSystem, createDummyFileSystem) is entirely unimplemented in this FOSS build — every method throws.
Scene.save is functional for direct file I/O but the FileSystem abstraction it relies on is unimplemented.
A3DObject represents the base class for all 3D objects in Aspose.3D FOSS for TypeScript.
AnimationChannel defines a single animation channel that controls how animation data is applied over time.
AnimationClip holds a collection of animation channels that together represent a complete animation sequence.
AnimationNode represents a node in the animation system that can be animated using keyframes or other animation data.
ApertureMode specifies how the camera aperture is defined in rendering settings.
AssetInfo stores metadata about a 3D asset such as author, creation date, and units.
BindPoint defines a binding location for skinning or other skeletal animations.
BooleanOperation represents a boolean operation such as union, intersection, or difference between two geometries.
BoundingBox describes the three-dimensional bounding volume of an object using minimum and maximum coordinates.
BoundingBox2D describes the two-dimensional bounding volume of an object using minimum and maximum coordinates.
BoundingBoxExtent provides the size and center of a bounding box.
Camera defines a view frustum and projection settings for rendering a 3D scene.
ComposeOrder specifies the order in which transformations are applied during composition.
CustomObject allows users to define and embed custom 3D objects with specific properties.
Entity is the base class for all 3D entities such as meshes, lights, and cameras.
Extrapolation defines how animation values are computed outside the defined keyframe range.
ExtrapolationType specifies the method used to extrapolate animation values beyond keyframe boundaries.
FMatrix4 represents a 4x4 matrix of single-precision floating-point numbers used for transformations.
FVector2 represents a two-dimensional vector of single-precision floating-point numbers.
FVector3 represents a three-dimensional vector of single-precision floating-point numbers.
FVector4 represents a four-dimensional vector of single-precision floating-point numbers.
FileFormat identifies the format of a 3D file such as OBJ, STL, or GLTF.
FileSystem provides an abstraction layer for file and directory operations.
Geometry defines the shape of a 3D object through vertices, indices, and other topological data.
GlobalTransform stores the absolute transformation matrix of an object in world space.
IIndexedVertexElement represents an indexed vertex element used in mesh rendering.
INamedObject is an interface for objects that have a name property.
IOExtension provides support for loading and saving 3D files in various formats.
ImageRenderOptions controls how a 3D scene is rendered to an image.
Interpolation defines the method used to calculate values between keyframes.
KeyFrame represents a single keyframe in an animation sequence with a time and value.
KeyframeSequence holds a sequence of keyframes that define an animation curve.
LambertMaterial defines a simple diffuse lighting material based on the Lambertian reflectance model.
Light defines a light source in a 3D scene with configurable properties such as color and intensity.
LightType specifies the kind of light such as point, directional, or spot.
MappingMode defines how texture coordinates are mapped onto a surface.
Material defines the visual appearance of a 3D object through surface properties.
MathUtils provides utility functions for common mathematical operations used in 3D graphics.
Matrix4 represents a 4x4 matrix of double-precision floating-point numbers used for transformations.
Mesh represents a polygonal mesh composed of vertices, edges, and faces.
Node represents an object in a scene hierarchy that can hold geometry and other entities.
ParseException indicates an error that occurred while parsing a 3D file format.
PbrMaterial defines a physically based rendering material with properties such as base color, metallic factor, and roughness.
PhongMaterial defines a Phong shading material with properties such as ambient, diffuse, and specular colors.
PolygonModifier provides utilities for modifying polygonal geometry, such as triangulation.
ProjectionType specifies the type of projection used in a camera, such as perspective or orthographic.
Property represents a named value that can be attached to scene objects for metadata.
PropertyCollection is a container for a set of properties associated with a scene object.
Quaternion represents a four-dimensional vector used to describe 3D rotations.
Rect defines a rectangle using left, top, width, and height values.
ReferenceMode specifies how a reference to another object is interpreted during import or export.
RelativeRectangle defines a rectangle using relative coordinates and dimensions.
RotationMode specifies the method used to interpret rotation values.
RotationOrder defines the sequence in which rotations around the X, Y, and Z axes are applied.
Scene represents a complete 3D scene containing nodes, entities, and materials.
SceneObject is the base class for all objects that can be part of a 3D scene.
SemanticAttribute defines the meaning of a vertex attribute, such as position or normal.
SplitMeshPolicy specifies how meshes should be split during export or processing.
StepMode defines how vertex data is advanced per vertex or per instance during rendering.
TextureMapping specifies how a texture is mapped onto a surface.
Transform represents a 4x4 matrix used to apply translation, rotation, and scaling to objects.
TransformBuilder provides a fluent interface for constructing transformation matrices.
Vector2 represents a two-dimensional vector with X and Y components.
Vector3 represents a three-dimensional vector with X, Y, and Z components.
Vector4 represents a four-dimensional vector with X, Y, Z, and W components.
Vertex represents a single point in a mesh with associated attributes such as position and normal.
VertexDeclaration describes the layout of vertex data for rendering.
VertexElement is the base class for individual components of a vertex, such as position or normal.
VertexElementFVector represents a vertex element containing floating-point vector data.
VertexElementIntsTemplate represents a vertex element containing integer data.
VertexElementNormal represents a vertex element containing normal vector data.
VertexElementSmoothingGroup represents a vertex element containing smoothing group information.
VertexElementTangent represents a vertex element containing tangent vector data.
VertexElementType specifies the data type of a vertex element, such as float or integer.
VertexElementUV represents a vertex element containing texture coordinate data.
VertexElementVertexColor represents a vertex element containing vertex color data.
VertexField defines a named field within a vertex declaration.
VertexFieldDataType specifies the data type of a vertex field, such as float3 or uint8.
VertexFieldSemantic defines the semantic meaning of a vertex field, such as position or color.
Watermark represents a visual overlay that can be added to exported 3D files.
WeightedMode represents a weighting strategy used in mesh processing operations.
